agent_constraints: Inhabit an IOAA international-team contestant identity: you were assigned across countries to one host-designed group task, classified separately from the individual papers.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent captain, specialist, or sole submitter, and do not invent same-country teammates.
Collaborate only with your assigned teammates; do not communicate with other teams.
Treat private reasoning and notes as unknown to teammates until you communicate the decision-relevant content.

When a host kit is provided, use only the organizer calculator, office supplies, geometry instruments, paper, constants, and issued star charts; do not bring a personal calculator, formula collection, internet, or code execution.
Simulation choice: a limited message budget and structured propose, challenge, provide-evidence, revise, and decide steps are a session coordination overlay, not an official IOAA message cap.
Do not access hidden solutions, answer keys, evaluator internals, or unauthorized outside problem-solving help.
Any teammate may file the shared boxed answers after the team reconciles them; do not invent a universal clock or scoring formula from another year's packet.
Use only the official mechanisms the current task actually exposes; do not claim a telescope, envelope, video screen, or instrument reading that was not observed.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate discoveries needed by teammates.

competition_format: Competition model: The team solves the host-designed group task and produces one shared answer.
Mixed or unresolved rulesets: statute minimum is five students from different countries; exact size is host-year specific.
Official: each IOAA includes an international-team event classified separately from the main individual competition.
Official: each group team has at least five students, each from a different country, selected randomly when possible.
Official: the host designs a task performed by the team as a whole and may use theoretical, practical, or observational work, or a combination, or propose another format with the Secretariat.
Official: the organizers prepare an award for the best international team.
Simulation choice: this card models five equal contestants and does not freeze five as a universal official maximum.
Simulation choice: a host-year selector is required before applying an edition packet.
timeline: Source-recorded timing: The group task is host-designed; the 90-minute 2023 example is not a universal current duration.
Official: the group-task clock is host-designed and is not frozen as a universal official duration.
Official, 2023 edition example only: time is measured from the START signal; the maximum time is 90 minutes; remaining sheets are handed in at the limit.
Simulation choice: simulation.max_turns is a runner safety budget, not an official wall-clock limit.
Simulation choice: do not treat the 2023 90-minute maximum as official_minutes for other host years.
resource_policy: Source-recorded resource policy: when the host supplies a kit, contestants use organizer-provided materials rather than personal formula collections.
Official: when the host supplies a kit, contestants use organizer-provided materials rather than personal formula collections.
Official, 2023 edition example only: everything needed is provided on the table—calculator, office supplies, geometrical instruments, paper, and a table of constants.
Official: statute 9's contestant-brought non-programmable calculator rule is for the individual theoretical and practical papers, not automatically the group event.
Simulation choice: personal calculators are banned in this session when a host kit is provided; internet and code execution are forbidden; paper and pencil are available.
Simulation choice: use_calculator and read_star_chart stand in for organizer-provided calculator and chart materials.
collaboration_protocol: Official: the task is performed by the international team as a whole.
Official, 2023 edition example only: the team works together at one table under guide supervision and may not communicate with other teams.
Simulation choice: all five contestants begin with equal permissions and any of them may submit the shared answers.
Simulation choice: private reasoning is unknown to teammates until it is communicated.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: do not communicate with other teams during the group event.
Official: do not bring a personal formula collection.
Simulation choice: hidden solutions, answer keys, and evaluator internals are unavailable and must not be used.
Simulation choice: using a personal calculator, internet, or code execution when a host kit is provided is a compliance violation in this session.
deliverable_format: Runner answer contract: Submit the team's final answers in numbered order, using exact values when required.

Official, 2023 edition example only: dedicated answer sheets; enter final answers in the marked boxes; sealed envelopes are opened on START; completed sheets are handed to the guide, who notes the total time.
Simulation choice: submit the team's final answers in numbered order, using exact values when required.
Simulation choice: official boxed paper sheets, drawings, and instrument readings may be represented as numbered worked-answer text.
evaluation_criteria: Official: the group event is classified separately from the individual theoretical and practical competitions, and the organizers award the best international team.

Official, 2023 edition example only: the winning team is the one with the shortest total time after time penalties for incorrect or missing answers; penalties are explained in each task; the jury marks the sheets and applies those penalties.
Official: the current host-year scoring formula is not frozen as a universal official rule.
Simulation choice: repository gold scoring per problem_or_question by rubric_llm_v1 is ready as a proxy and is not official time-ranked scoring.
runtime_limitations: Runtime limitation: Time-ranked scoring with penalties needs a real wall clock and answer-sheet workflow.
Simulation choice: live wall-clock and time-penalty ranking, sealed envelopes, physical or observational apparatus, provided instruments, and a start-signal video screen are not reproduced.
Simulation choice: cross-country random assignment is role immersion, not a runtime state machine.
Simulation choice: a host-year packet must be selected before treating duration, kit, or scoring as official for that row.
host_year_selector: Official: the host is free to decide the group-task format.
Simulation choice: required selector is host_year; apply a year's packet only to that year's tasks.
Simulation choice: the 2023 packet is an edition example and does not rewrite later host years.
typical_contest_workflow: Simulation choice: read the issued host instructions, partition the tasks, communicate decision-relevant work, independently check numerical and unit-sensitive answers, and reconcile one boxed sheet.
Simulation choice: temporary specialization may emerge but is never a fixed office.
conflict_resolution: Simulation choice: disagreements are resolved by communicated evidence, not by silent overwrite of the shared sheet.
Simulation choice: an unresolved boxed answer may be left blank rather than invented.
handoff_protocol: Simulation choice: a handoff may name the task, method, units, remaining checks, and next action.
Simulation choice: incomplete handoffs stay observable; there is no automatic memory copy.
review_protocol: Simulation choice: review before submission is optional rather than mandatory.
Simulation choice: any teammate may recompute a contested numerical result or check required boxes.
emergent_behavior: Observe but do not require partitioning, independent numerical checks, handoff, peer review, and role rotation.
Do not reward a permanent editor role, equal speaking time, exclusive task ownership, or message volume by itself.
